summary.plain: A tank of dry-cleaning fluid nearly a mile underground in a South Dakota gold mine, run for decades by Ray Davis, that made the first direct detection of solar neutrinos and found far fewer than expected — a puzzle not solved for thirty years.
summary.technical: Radiochemical chlorine-argon solar-neutrino experiment in the Homestake Gold Mine, Lead, South Dakota, 1478 m (4850 ft) underground; 380 m3 (100,000 gal) perchloroethylene target. Operated continuously 1970-1994, measuring a 37Ar production rate of 2.56±0.16(stat)±0.16(syst) SNU, about one-third of the Standard Solar Model prediction -- the original 'solar neutrino problem', later resolved by neutrino oscillation (SNO, Super-Kamiokande).
